title: publish the branch and record what the Windows workflow actually says
action: The three preceding cells fixed what could be fixed and proved what could be proved on a POSIX machine. The one claim none of them can make is about Windows. This cell obtains that evidence: push the branch so the Windows workflow runs against the fix, then record what it actually reports — not what it was hoped to report. Capture, per suite: which of the previously-failing three now pass, which still fail, and for anything still failing, the actual error rather than a restatement of the earlier diagnosis. The four standing exclusions are still in place, so this run says nothing about them; what it can say is whether the gitdir identity fix cleared the merge-queue timeout chain and whether the two repaired workflow steps now execute. If the run is still red, that is the result — record it with the failing output and file what it reveals, since a wrong prediction recorded honestly is worth more than a green claimed early.

truths: the branch is pushed and the Windows workflow run triggered by it is identified by id
the run's outcome is recorded per suite, with actual failing output quoted for anything still red
the report distinguishes what this run proves (the diagnosed cause, the repaired steps) from what it cannot (the four still-excluded suites)
key_links: wpi-1 fixed the one diagnosed cause; this run is its only real proof
prohibitions: Never report a green that the run did not produce
Never remove an exclusion on the strength of this run without the suite itself passing

verify: gh run list --branch main --workflow Windows --limit 1 --json conclusion,databaseId
